claims.text: The nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst initially has a disordered surface atomic structure.
The controlled intervention is to vary the ethanol-to-water vapor ratio from 5% ethanol to as much as 50% ethanol.
Increasing ethanol partial pressure increases the surface coverage of ethanol.
Increasing ethanol partial pressure increases the surface coverage of ethanol-reaction intermediates.
Greater adsorbate coverage drives reversible rearrangement of surface atoms.
Adsorbate-induced surface reconstruction modifies the ensemble of catalytic active sites.
Surface reconstruction shifts the electronic properties of the active sites, potentially including their d-band center.
The reconstructed active sites have altered adsorption energies for species involved in ethanol oxidation.
The reconstructed active sites alter the kinetics of subsequent ethanol-oxidation steps.
The reconstruction-induced changes in adsorption and kinetics alter catalytic activity.
The reconstruction-induced changes in adsorption and kinetics alter product selectivity.
Relative to 5% ethanol, higher ethanol partial pressures will change the steady-state current density.
Relative to 5% ethanol, higher ethanol partial pressures will shift the product distribution.
In-situ characterization will reveal surface atomic rearrangement concomitant with the performance changes.
At the 5% ethanol baseline, adsorbate-induced restructuring is expected to be minimal.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at 80°C, constant potential, and ethanol partial pressures up to 50%.
Conditions involving excessive adsorption or catalyst degradation fall outside the proposed mechanism's valid regime.
